summary: The v3 engraving case matches 14/24 screens. After walking away from and back to the starting square, key E at step 14 is refused by js/engrave.js u_can_engrave() because it admits only ROOM/CORR and checks floor reachability before the stylus prompt. C engrave.c u_can_engrave() tests the source terrain categories with ACCESSIBLE() and does not test floor reachability there; C asks “What do you want to write with? [- ab or ?*]”. Port the whole source predicate and let doengrave apply later floor/stylus rules in their C order.

source.branch: A sighted Valkyrie returns to her initial square after east/west movement and invokes E/engrave. C u_can_engrave() finds the square accessible, the hero able to wield and within capacity, then doengrave() prompts for a stylus. JS rejects before the prompt because its u_can_engrave() subset requires ROOM or CORR and can_reach_floor() at entry.
callers: engrave.c doengrave() at lines 956-968 calls u_can_engrave() and returns ECMD_FAIL only when it returns false; js/engrave.js doengrave() calls the partial predicate before selecting a writing implement.
cmd.c E/engrave dispatch reaches doengrave(); the v3 recording proves this path at segment 0 step 14.
dependencies: Match C SURFACE_AT/ACCESSIBLE terrain test, engulfed animal/whirly text, lava/pool/fountain/air/solid rejection, cantwield() and check_capacity() return values. Do not move the later can_reach_floor() rule from doengrave() into the early predicate.

The later bare-fingertip repeat-engraving path is still guarded by js/engrave.js doengrave() when an engraving exists; after the first predicate fix, replay may expose that separate source-owned branch.

evidence: Saved challenges/evaluations/20260925191954-v3.json at 7dd208a68ee62546cb117c2d9763f8e1e63fef62 reports 14/24 screens and cursors, 3016/3016 RNG calls, and 10 unmatched screens.

Current diagnostic .cache/loop-v3-fingertip-engraving-diagnostic.json at 4151ee7a2286fbfce141545c893e052e0c49a44d stops at segment 0 step 14 key E with “engrave requires an accessible ordinary floor”; C asks for the writing implement instead.

C recording challenges/cases/v3/fingertip-engraving-return.session.json shows step 12 east, step 13 west, step 14 E prompting “What do you want to write with? [- ab or ?*]”, and step 15 key - writing in dust. This is a repeated engraving after returning to the initial square.

nethack-c/upstream/src/engrave.c u_can_engrave() at 503-541 tests swallowed, lava, pool/fountain, air and !ACCESSIBLE() terrain, then cantwield and check_capacity. It does not limit terrain to ROOM/CORR or call can_reach_floor at this point; doengrave() calls it at line 963 and tests can_reach_floor later after choosing a stylus.

js/engrave.js u_can_engrave() near line 204 throws when typ is outside ROOM/CORR or can_reach_floor() is false, before doengrave() can prompt. Its doengrave() remains a documented partial bare-fingertip implementation with a separate existing-engraving guard.
